questions.text: Under the approximate dense-training compute relation C=6ND, what happens to C if both parameter count N and training-token count D double?
questions.explanation: Multiplying both N and D by2 multiplies their product, and hence C, by4.

questions.text: Two training plans have parameter/token counts (N,D) and (N/4,4D). Under C≈6ND, how do their training-compute estimates compare?

options.A: The second needs one quarter as much compute.
options.B: The second needs four times as much compute.
options.C: The second needs sixteen times as much compute.
options.D: They have the same estimated training compute.

questions.explanation: (N/4)*(4D)=ND, so the compute estimate is unchanged.
